scored.context:
[1] RMC NO. 38-2026, p.3 (2026) · OCR
6. To ensure consistent and proper online display of the BER Registration Seal Badge on
websites, mobile applications, online shops and e-commerce platforms, the following
guidelines shall apply:

6.1 Only the BIR Registration Seal Badge shall be posted on the taxpayer’s official
website, mobile application, online shop, or e-commerce platform profile page. (refer
to Annex B).

6.2 Taxpayers are not required to upload their entire registration document or the full page
where the badge appears. Taxpayers may crop, scan, or extract only the BIR
Registration Seal Badge image for the purpose of uploading or posting it to their
official website, mobile application, online shop, or e-commerce platform profile

There shall be levied, as sessed and collected a tax equivalent to twenty percent (20%) based on the wholesale price, net of Excise and Value-Added Tax (VAT), for locally manufactured perfumes and toilet waters. ---

scored.query: What is the annual gross sales limit to qualify as a Micro Taxpayer under the Ease of Paying Taxes Act?
scored.context:
[1] RR 8-2024, p.1 (2024)
REVENUE REGULATIONS NO. 8-2024 issued on April 11, 2024, implements Section 21(b) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended by Republic Act No. 11976 (Ease of Paying Taxes Act), on the classification of taxpayers. Taxpayers shall be classified, and be covered by these Regulations, as follows: A. Micro Taxpayer – shall refer to a taxpayer whose gross sales for a taxable year is less than Three Million Pesos (₱3,000,000.00). B. Small Taxpayer - shall refer to a taxpayer whose gross sales for a taxable year is Three Million Pesos (₱3,000,000.00) to less than Twenty Million Pesos (₱20,000,000.00). C. Medium Taxpayer - shall refer to a taxpayer whose gross sales for a taxable year is Twenty Million Pesos (₱20,000,000.00) to less than One Billion Pesos (₱1,000,000,000.00).

---

[2] RR 8-2024, p.1 (2024)
C. Medium Taxpayer - shall refer to a taxpayer whose gross sales for a taxable year is Twenty Million Pesos (₱20,000,000.00) to less than One Billion Pesos (₱1,000,000,000.00). D. Large Taxpayer - shall refer to a taxpayer whose gross sales for a taxable year is One Billion Pesos (₱1,000,000,000.00) and above. For purposes of classification of taxpayers under these Regulations, gross sales shall refer to total sales revenue, net of VAT, if applicable, during the taxable year, without any other deductions. Gross sales shall only cover business income, excluding compensation income earned under employer-employee relationship, passive income under Sections 24, 25, 27 and 28, and income excluded under Section 32(B), all of the Tax Code.

---

[3] RR 8-2024, p.1 (2024)
Taxpayers registered in 2022 and prior years shall be classified based on gross sales for taxable year 2022. For taxpayers registered in 2022 and prior years but without any submitted information on their gross sales for taxable year 2022, and taxpayers registered in 2023 or in 2024 before the effectivity of the Regulations, shall initially be classified as MICRO, except VAT-registered taxpayers, who shall be classified as SMALL.
scored.answer:

- Gross sales means total sales revenue, net of VAT if applicable, with no other deductions, and covers business income only [2].
- Taxpayers registered in 2023 or 2024 before the Regulations took effect are initially classified as MICRO, except VAT-registered taxpayers, who are classified as SMALL [3].

scored.answer:
Oo, may kinakaltas na withholding tax ang mga e-marketplace operator sa mga ibinabayad sa kanilang online sellers. Sa ilalim ng RR 16-2023, **1%** ang rate na ipinapataw sa kalahati (1/2) ng gross remittances ng e-marketplace operators at digital financial services providers sa mga seller/merchant [1].

Pero kapag lumampas sa ₱500,000 sa anumang oras ng taxable year, awtomatikong ibabawas ang withholding tax sa remittance na lumampas sa threshold at sa mga susunod pang remittance [2][3].

row.query: Has the BIR established a mandatory floor price for selling cigarettes and vape products?

- Heated tobacco products: **₱120.40** floor price per pack of 20 sticks [1].
- Vapor products (nicotine salt): **₱200.00** for a 1x2ml pod and **₱354.97** for a 1x4ml pod [1].
- Vapor products (freebase/classic nicotine): **₱179.20** for a 1x10ml bottle and **₱403.20** for a 1x30ml bottle [2].

The documents don't state a separate floor price for conventional cigarettes.

The rules shall apply to donations consisting purely of cash, made during the same calendar year, to natural or juridical persons, including organizations, foundations, and institutions. Donor's Tax return for purely cash donations shall be filed electronically in any of the available electronic platforms [e.g., eBIRForms Facility, Electronic Filing and Payment System (eFPS), tax returns filing applications/solutions of Authorized Taxpayer Service Providers (ATSPs)].

e. Certificate of Donation (for tax-exempt donee); f. For cash donations made to accredited Donee Institutions under Section 34(H) of the Tax Code, the aforesaid documents shall serve as evidence of the transaction to support future claims for deductions from gross income, in addition to the Philippine Council for NGO Certification (PCNC) Accreditation issued by the BIR to the Donee. scored.answer:
Under RMC No. 10-2026, donations consisting purely of cash made during the same calendar year to natural or juridical persons (including organizations, foundations, and institutions) are covered by clarified rules on tax treatment, documentation, and filing/payment of Donor's Tax [2].

- The Donor's Tax return must be filed **electronically** through any available platform, such as eBIRForms, eFPS, or ATSP filing applications [2].
- Documentary requirements (e.g., notarized Deed of Donation, proof of cash transfer, proof of filing of BIR Form No. 1800, proof of payment, Certificate of Donation for tax-exempt donees, IDs, and TINs) must be submitted within **30 days** after the gift is made or completed to the RDO having jurisdiction over the Donor's residence/registration, or to the LT Division for large taxpayers [1][3].
- An **eCAR is not required** for purely cash donations, since cash is not registrable property [3].

The documents don't cover the specific donor's tax rates or exemptions applicable.

scored.query: Does the cross-border doctrine still apply to ecozones for VAT zero-rating purposes?
scored.context:
[1] RMC No. 24-2022, p.1 (2022)
The "cross border doctrine" as applied to Ecozones or Freeport zones has been rendered ineffectual and inoperative for VAT purposes with the passage of CREATE Act because of the following: a. Passage of RA No. 11534, or the CREATE Act, expressly providing that only those goods and services that are directly and exclusively used in the registered project or activity of Registered Business Enterprises (RBEs) qualify as VAT 0% local purchases; b. Sections 294(E) and 295(D), Title Xlll of the Tax Code, as amended by the CREATE Act, and as implemented under Rule 2, Section 5, and Rule 18, Section 5, respectively, of the CREATE IRR, stating certain parameters for the availment of VAT zero-rating on local purchases of registered export enterprises, regardless of location;

---

[2] RMC No. 24-2022, p.1 (2022)
Thus, following the "cross border doctrine", the sale of goods and services by a VAT-registered seller to registered enterprises in these economic and freeport zones were treated as constructive export subject to zero-percent (0%) VAT. The "cross border doctrine" as applied to Ecozones or Freeport zones has been rendered ineffectual and inoperative for VAT purposes with the passage of CREATE Act because of the following: a. Passage of RA No. 11534, or the CREATE Act, expressly providing that only those goods and services that are directly and exclusively used in the registered project or activity of Registered Business Enterprises (RBEs) qualify as VAT 0% local purchases;

---

[3] RMC No. 24-2022, p.1 (2022)
Before the CREATE Act, Ecozones and Freeportzones were, by legal fiction, regarded as foreign territories under Revenue Memorandum Circular (RMC) No. 74-99 and RMC No. 7-2007. Thus, following the "cross border doctrine", the sale of goods and services by a VAT-registered seller to registered enterprises in these economic and freeport zones were treated as constructive export subject to zero-percent (0%) VAT.
scored.answer:
No — the cross-border doctrine no longer applies to Ecozones or Freeport zones for VAT zero-rating purposes. RMC No. 24-2022 states that the doctrine "has been rendered ineffectual and inoperative for VAT purposes with the passage of CREATE Act" [1][2].

- Before CREATE, these zones were treated by legal fiction as foreign territories, so sales to registered enterprises there were treated as constructive exports subject to 0% VAT [3].
- Under the CREATE Act, only goods and services directly and exclusively used in the registered project or activity of a Registered Business Enterprise qualify as VAT 0% local purchases, regardless of location [1][2].

row.query: Umiiral pa ba ang cross-border doctrine para sa VAT zero-rating sa loob ng mga ecozone?

sagot.answer:
Hindi na. Sa ilalim ng RMC No. 24-2022, ang "cross border doctrine" para sa mga Ecozone o Freeport zone ay itinuturing nang **ineffectual at inoperative** para sa VAT purposes dahil sa pagpasa ng CREATE Act (RA No. 11534) [1][2].

- Bago ang CREATE Act, ang mga Ecozone at Freeport zone ay itinuturing na foreign territories, kaya ang mga benta rito ay constructive export na may 0% VAT [3].
- Sa ilalim ng CREATE Act, tanging mga goods at services na **direkta at eksklusibong ginagamit** sa registered project o activity ng Registered Business Enterprise (RBE) ang kwalipikado sa VAT 0% local purchases [1][2].
sagot.context:
[1] RMC No. 24-2022, p.1 (2022)
The "cross border doctrine" as applied to Ecozones or Freeport zones has been rendered ineffectual and inoperative for VAT purposes with the passage of CREATE Act because of the following: a. Passage of RA No. 11534, or the CREATE Act, expressly providing that only those goods and services that are directly and exclusively used in the registered project or activity of Registered Business Enterprises (RBEs) qualify as VAT 0% local purchases; b. Sections 294(E) and 295(D), Title Xlll of the Tax Code, as amended by the CREATE Act, and as implemented under Rule 2, Section 5, and Rule 18, Section 5, respectively, of the CREATE IRR, stating certain parameters for the availment of VAT zero-rating on local purchases of registered export enterprises, regardless of location;

---

[2] RMC No. 24-2022, p.1 (2022)
Thus, following the "cross border doctrine", the sale of goods and services by a VAT-registered seller to registered enterprises in these economic and freeport zones were treated as constructive export subject to zero-percent (0%) VAT. The "cross border doctrine" as applied to Ecozones or Freeport zones has been rendered ineffectual and inoperative for VAT purposes with the passage of CREATE Act because of the following: a. Passage of RA No. 11534, or the CREATE Act, expressly providing that only those goods and services that are directly and exclusively used in the registered project or activity of Registered Business Enterprises (RBEs) qualify as VAT 0% local purchases;

---

[3] RMC No. 24-2022, p.1 (2022)
Before the CREATE Act, Ecozones and Freeportzones were, by legal fiction, regarded as foreign territories under Revenue Memorandum Circular (RMC) No. 74-99 and RMC No. 7-2007. Thus, following the "cross border doctrine", the sale of goods and services by a VAT-registered seller to registered enterprises in these economic and freeport zones were treated as constructive export subject to zero-percent (0%) VAT.

For purposes of claiming the output VAT credit on uncollected receivables, the customer/buyer must be properly identified in the Summary List of Sales in the quarter when the sale was made. However, if the seller lumps all sales into one " various" account entry, the lumping shall be considered invalid compliance with the requisites provided for purposes of claiming the output VAT credit on uncollected receivables and the output VAT cannot be used or allowed as VAT Credit should the transaction remain uncollected after the lapse of the agreed period to pay. scored.query: Pwede bang mag-claim ng output VAT credit ang taxpayer sa mga hindi nakolektang utang sa ilalim ng Ease of Paying Taxes Act?
scored.context:
[1] RMC No. 65-2024 Digest, p.3 (2024)
For purposes of claiming the output VAT credit on uncollected receivables, the customer/buyer must be properly identified in the Summary List of Sales in the quarter when the sale was made. However, if the seller lumps all sales into one " various" account entry, the lumping shall be considered invalid compliance with the requisites provided for purposes of claiming the output VAT credit on uncollected receivables and the output VAT cannot be used or allowed as VAT Credit should the transaction remain uncollected after the lapse of the agreed period to pay. The following taxpayers are disqualified to avail output VAT tax credit on uncollected receivables: a. Those tagged as cannot be located (CBL) taxpayers;

---

[2] RMC No. 65-2024 Digest, p.3 (2024)
a. Those tagged as cannot be located (CBL) taxpayers; b. Those with duly filed complaints at the DOJ under the Run After Fake Transaction (RAFT) and Run After Tax Evaders (RATE) programs; c. Other taxpayers that may be identified by the Commissioner. If the goods were returned during the agreed upon period to pay and the output VAT is not yet paid, the return is treated as a sales return and therefore a deduction from gross sales in the quarter where the goods were returned. If the goods were returned and accepted by the seller but the claim for output VAT credit has been made, it is treated as sales return but for purposes of VAT, no deduction on sales and output VAT shall be allowed since the claim for output VAT credit has already been made.

---

[3] RMC No. 65-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
Only the seller of goods and/or services may deduct output VAT credit which corresponds to the uncollected receivables originating from the sales on account that transpired upon the effectivity of RR No. 3-2024 from the output VAT of the next quarter after the lapse of the agreed upon period to pay. Before a seller can credit the VAT paid on the uncollected receivables, the following requisites must be present: a. The sale or exchange has taken place after the effectivity of RR No. 3-2024; b. The sale is on credit or on account; c. There is a written agreement on the period to pay the receivable, i.e. credit term is indicated on the invoice or any document showing the credit term; d. The VAT is separately shown on the invoice;
scored.answer:
Oo, pwede — sa ilalim ng RMC No. 65-2024, ang nagbebenta ng goods at/o services lang ang maaaring mag-deduct ng output VAT credit na katumbas ng mga hindi nakolektang receivable mula sa mga sales on account na nangyari pagkatapos maging epektibo ang RR No. 3-2024 [3].

Kailangang matugunan ang mga requisites: nangyari ang sale pagkatapos ng effectivity ng RR No. 3-2024, ang sale ay on credit o on account, may written agreement sa period to pay, at ang VAT ay hiwalay na nakasaad sa invoice [3].

row.query: Kailangan bang isama ng mga distribution utility sa kuryente ang mga third-party pass-through charges sa kanilang gross sales?

sagot.answer:
Hindi. Sa ilalim ng RMC No. 116-2024, ang gross sales ng mga Distribution Utility (DU) at Electric Cooperative (EC) para sa pagbebenta ng kuryente ay **hindi kasama** ang VAT at ang mga halagang nakalaan para sa pagbabayad sa third party o natanggap bilang reimbursement sa pagbabayad para sa iba, na hindi napupunta sa seller [1][2].

- Ang mga DU/EC ay hindi rin maaaring mag-claim ng Input Tax mula sa mga ito [1][3].
- Ang tamang claimant ng Input Tax ay ang mga customer na may negosyo, base sa invoice na ibibigay ng DU/EC [3].

scored.query: What is the preferential corporate income tax rate for non-profit proprietary educational institutions?
scored.context:
[1] RR 3-2022, p.1 (2022)
REVENUE REGULATIONS NO. 3-2022 issued on April 8, 2022 implements the provisions of Republic Act (RA) No. 11635, titled “An Act Amending Section 27 (B) of the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC) of 1997, as Amended, and for Other Purposes” on the income taxation of proprietary educational institutions and hospitals which are non-profit. The following institutions shall be covered by the preferential ten percent (10%) Corporate Income Tax rate; Provided, that beginning July 1, 2020 until June 30, 2023, the rate of one percent (1%) shall apply, as imposed under Section 27 (B) of the NIRC, as amended: a. Proprietary Educational Institutions; b. Hospitals which are non-profit;

---

[2] RR 3-2022, p.1 (2022)
b. Hospitals which are non-profit; and, c. Non-Stock, Non-Profit Educational Institutions whose net income or assets accrue/inure to or benefit any member or specific person. After June 30, 2023, the rate shall revert to the preferential Corporate Income Tax rate of 10%. The twenty-five percent (25%) regular Corporate Income Tax rate prescribed under Section 27(A) of the NIRC, as amended, shall be imposed on the entire taxable income of the institutions mentioned in Section 3 of the Regulations , if their gross income from unrelated trade, business or other activity, as defined herein, exceeds fifty percent (50%) of the total gross income they derived from all sources.

---

[3] RR 3-2022, p.1 (2022)
The twenty-five percent (25%) regular Corporate Income Tax rate prescribed under Section 27(A) of the NIRC, as amended, shall be imposed on the entire taxable income of the institutions mentioned in Section 3 of the Regulations , if their gross income from unrelated trade, business or other activity, as defined herein, exceeds fifty percent (50%) of the total gross income they derived from all sources. Moreover, a Non-Stock, Non-Profit Educational Institution, not falling under Section 3 of these Regulations, shall be subject to the rate of twenty-five percent (25%) regular Corporate Income Tax on the portion of its revenues or assets not used actually, directly, and exclusively for educational purposes, as provided in Section 27(A) of the NIRC, as amended.
scored.answer: The preferential corporate income tax rate for non-profit proprietary educational institutions is **10%** [1]. However, from **July 1, 2020 until June 30, 2023**, the rate was **1%**; after June 30, 2023, it reverts to **10%** [1][2].

sagot.answer: Sa ilalim ng RR 3-2022, ang preferential corporate income tax rate para sa mga non-profit proprietary educational institutions ay **10%** [1]. Gayunpaman, mula **July 1, 2020 hanggang June 30, 2023**, ang rate na **1%** ang ipinapatupad [1]. Pagkatapos ng June 30, 2023, babalik ito sa **10%** [2].
sagot.context:
[1] RR 3-2022, p.1 (2022)
REVENUE REGULATIONS NO. 3-2022 issued on April 8, 2022 implements the provisions of Republic Act (RA) No. 11635, titled “An Act Amending Section 27 (B) of the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC) of 1997, as Amended, and for Other Purposes” on the income taxation of proprietary educational institutions and hospitals which are non-profit. The following institutions shall be covered by the preferential ten percent (10%) Corporate Income Tax rate; Provided, that beginning July 1, 2020 until June 30, 2023, the rate of one percent (1%) shall apply, as imposed under Section 27 (B) of the NIRC, as amended: a. Proprietary Educational Institutions; b. Hospitals which are non-profit;

---

[2] RR 3-2022, p.1 (2022)
b. Hospitals which are non-profit; and, c. Non-Stock, Non-Profit Educational Institutions whose net income or assets accrue/inure to or benefit any member or specific person. After June 30, 2023, the rate shall revert to the preferential Corporate Income Tax rate of 10%. The twenty-five percent (25%) regular Corporate Income Tax rate prescribed under Section 27(A) of the NIRC, as amended, shall be imposed on the entire taxable income of the institutions mentioned in Section 3 of the Regulations , if their gross income from unrelated trade, business or other activity, as defined herein, exceeds fifty percent (50%) of the total gross income they derived from all sources.

---

Moreover, a Non-Stock, Non-Profit Educational Institution, not falling under Section 3 of these Regulations, shall be subject to the rate of twenty-five percent (25%) regular Corporate Income Tax on the portion of its revenues or assets not used actually, directly, and exclusively for educational purposes, as provided in Section 27(A) of the NIRC, as amended.

scored.query: Are Sukuk or Islamic bonds treated neutrally compared to conventional bonds for tax purposes?
scored.context:
[1] RMC No. 81-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
Any disposal or lease of the underlying asset, and execution of any additional instrument required in a Sukuk transaction, for the purpose of compliance with Shari'ah principles but which will not be required in a conventional bond transaction, shall be deemed excluded for taxation purposes. A Documentary Stamp Tax (DST) is imposed on all Sukuk instruments under Sections 176 and 179 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, (Tax Code) unless excepted under Section 199(g) of the same code. Guidelines and examples of some Sukuk structures that may be encountered in practice are provided in the Circular.

---

[2] RMC No. 81-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
REVENUE MEMORANDUM CIRCULAR NO. 81-2024 issued on July 18, 2024 provides the tax treatment of Sukuk (Islamic Bond) as Islamic banking arrangement pursuant to the Tax Neutrality Provision of Republic Act No. 11439 (An Act Providing for the Regulation and Organization of Islamic Banks) as implemented by Revenue Regulations No. 17-2020. Sukuk issued, structured in a Shari'ah-compliant manner, but with economic characteristics similar to bonds, are subject to the taxes per the Circular. The gain or profit in Sukuk is determined based on the specific structure and terms of the Sukuk issuance. It can be calculated through profit-sharing ratios, rental income, mark-up or price differentials, or the sale of underlying assets.

---

[3] RMC No. 81-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
Gains or profits realized by Originator/Obligor, Arranger, Manager, and Underwriter from Sukuk transactions are subject to regular Income Tax and Value-Added Tax (VAT ) or Percentage Tax, whichever is applicable. Gains or profits realized by the Special Purpose Vehicle are subject to regular Income Tax but exempt from VAT. Any disposal or lease of the underlying asset, and execution of any additional instrument required in a Sukuk transaction, for the purpose of compliance with Shari'ah principles but which will not be required in a conventional bond transaction, shall be deemed excluded for taxation purposes.
scored.answer:
Yes — Sukuk (Islamic bonds) are treated neutrally compared to conventional bonds for tax purposes. RMC No. 81-2024 provides the tax treatment of Sukuk as an Islamic banking arrangement pursuant to the Tax Neutrality Provision of RA No. 11439, as implemented by RR No. 17-2020 [2].

- Sukuk structured in a Shari'ah-compliant manner but with economic characteristics similar to bonds are subject to the taxes per the Circular [2].
- Any disposal or lease of the underlying asset, and any additional instrument required only for Shari'ah compliance (not required in a conventional bond), is deemed excluded for taxation purposes [1][3].
- A DST is imposed on all Sukuk instruments under Sections 176 and 179 of the Tax Code unless excepted under Section 199(g) [1].

row.query: Are Sukuk or Islamic bonds treated neutrally compared to conventional bonds for tax purposes?

sagot.answer:
Yes — Sukuk (Islamic bonds) are treated neutrally compared to conventional bonds for tax purposes. RMC No. 81-2024 provides the tax treatment of Sukuk as an Islamic banking arrangement pursuant to the Tax Neutrality Provision of RA No. 11439, as implemented by RR No. 17-2020 [2].

- Sukuk structured in a Shari'ah-compliant manner but with economic characteristics similar to bonds are subject to the taxes per the Circular [2].
- Any disposal or lease of the underlying asset, and any additional instrument required only for Shari'ah compliance (not required in a conventional bond), is deemed excluded for taxation purposes [1][3].
- A DST is imposed on all Sukuk instruments under Sections 176 and 179 of the Tax Code unless excepted under Section 199(g) [1].
sagot.context:
[1] RMC No. 81-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
Any disposal or lease of the underlying asset, and execution of any additional instrument required in a Sukuk transaction, for the purpose of compliance with Shari'ah principles but which will not be required in a conventional bond transaction, shall be deemed excluded for taxation purposes. A Documentary Stamp Tax (DST) is imposed on all Sukuk instruments under Sections 176 and 179 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, (Tax Code) unless excepted under Section 199(g) of the same code. Guidelines and examples of some Sukuk structures that may be encountered in practice are provided in the Circular.

---

[2] RMC No. 81-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
REVENUE MEMORANDUM CIRCULAR NO. 81-2024 issued on July 18, 2024 provides the tax treatment of Sukuk (Islamic Bond) as Islamic banking arrangement pursuant to the Tax Neutrality Provision of Republic Act No. 11439 (An Act Providing for the Regulation and Organization of Islamic Banks) as implemented by Revenue Regulations No. 17-2020. Sukuk issued, structured in a Shari'ah-compliant manner, but with economic characteristics similar to bonds, are subject to the taxes per the Circular. The gain or profit in Sukuk is determined based on the specific structure and terms of the Sukuk issuance. It can be calculated through profit-sharing ratios, rental income, mark-up or price differentials, or the sale of underlying assets.

---

[3] RMC No. 81-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
Gains or profits realized by Originator/Obligor, Arranger, Manager, and Underwriter from Sukuk transactions are subject to regular Income Tax and Value-Added Tax (VAT ) or Percentage Tax, whichever is applicable. Gains or profits realized by the Special Purpose Vehicle are subject to regular Income Tax but exempt from VAT. Any disposal or lease of the underlying asset, and execution of any additional instrument required in a Sukuk transaction, for the purpose of compliance with Shari'ah principles but which will not be required in a conventional bond transaction, shall be deemed excluded for taxation purposes.

scored.query: Magkano ang taunang gross sales para maituring na Small Taxpayer sa ilalim ng RR 8-2024?
scored.context:
[1] RR 8-2024, p.1 (2024)
REVENUE REGULATIONS NO. 8-2024 issued on April 11, 2024, implements Section 21(b) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended by Republic Act No. 11976 (Ease of Paying Taxes Act), on the classification of taxpayers. Taxpayers shall be classified, and be covered by these Regulations, as follows: A. Micro Taxpayer – shall refer to a taxpayer whose gross sales for a taxable year is less than Three Million Pesos (₱3,000,000.00). B. Small Taxpayer - shall refer to a taxpayer whose gross sales for a taxable year is Three Million Pesos (₱3,000,000.00) to less than Twenty Million Pesos (₱20,000,000.00). C. Medium Taxpayer - shall refer to a taxpayer whose gross sales for a taxable year is Twenty Million Pesos (₱20,000,000.00) to less than One Billion Pesos (₱1,000,000,000.00).

---

[2] RR 8-2024, p.1 (2024)
C. Medium Taxpayer - shall refer to a taxpayer whose gross sales for a taxable year is Twenty Million Pesos (₱20,000,000.00) to less than One Billion Pesos (₱1,000,000,000.00). D. Large Taxpayer - shall refer to a taxpayer whose gross sales for a taxable year is One Billion Pesos (₱1,000,000,000.00) and above. For purposes of classification of taxpayers under these Regulations, gross sales shall refer to total sales revenue, net of VAT, if applicable, during the taxable year, without any other deductions. Gross sales shall only cover business income, excluding compensation income earned under employer-employee relationship, passive income under Sections 24, 25, 27 and 28, and income excluded under Section 32(B), all of the Tax Code.

---

[3] RR 8-2024, p.1 (2024)
Taxpayers registered in 2022 and prior years shall be classified based on gross sales for taxable year 2022. For taxpayers registered in 2022 and prior years but without any submitted information on their gross sales for taxable year 2022, and taxpayers registered in 2023 or in 2024 before the effectivity of the Regulations, shall initially be classified as MICRO, except VAT-registered taxpayers, who shall be classified as SMALL.
scored.answer:
Sa ilalim ng RR 8-2024, ang Small Taxpayer ay may taunang gross sales na **₱3,000,000.00 hanggang mas mababa sa ₱20,000,000.00** [1].

- Ang ₱3,000,000.00 pababa (mas mababa sa halagang ito) ay Micro Taxpayer [1].
- Ang gross sales ay tumutukoy sa total sales revenue, net ng VAT kung applicable, at business income lamang [2].

scored.query: Ano ang kondisyon para magamit ang Output VAT Credit sa mga uncollected receivables?
scored.context:
[1] RMC No. 65-2024 Digest, p.3 (2024)
For purposes of claiming the output VAT credit on uncollected receivables, the customer/buyer must be properly identified in the Summary List of Sales in the quarter when the sale was made. However, if the seller lumps all sales into one " various" account entry, the lumping shall be considered invalid compliance with the requisites provided for purposes of claiming the output VAT credit on uncollected receivables and the output VAT cannot be used or allowed as VAT Credit should the transaction remain uncollected after the lapse of the agreed period to pay. The following taxpayers are disqualified to avail output VAT tax credit on uncollected receivables: a. Those tagged as cannot be located (CBL) taxpayers;

---

[2] RMC No. 65-2024 Digest, p.2 (2024)
The preceding rules do not amend the conditions on the deductibility of bad debts expense in the income tax returns as provided in RR No. 25-2002. For purposes of claiming output VAT credit on uncollected receivables, mere lapse of the agreed upon period to pay even without any effort on the part of the seller to collect the sales on account shall entitle the seller of output VAT credit subject to the conditions under Q&A No. 4 in the Circular. The seller is not necessarily required to automatically credit the VAT paid every time there is an uncollected receivable due to the lapse of the agreed upon period especially so if the likelihood of collectability is high . Availing of the benefit under Section 110(D) of the Tax Code is merely an option.

---

[3] RMC No. 65-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
Only the seller of goods and/or services may deduct output VAT credit which corresponds to the uncollected receivables originating from the sales on account that transpired upon the effectivity of RR No. 3-2024 from the output VAT of the next quarter after the lapse of the agreed upon period to pay. Before a seller can credit the VAT paid on the uncollected receivables, the following requisites must be present: a. The sale or exchange has taken place after the effectivity of RR No. 3-2024; b. The sale is on credit or on account; c. There is a written agreement on the period to pay the receivable, i.e. credit term is indicated on the invoice or any document showing the credit term; d. The VAT is separately shown on the invoice;
scored.answer:
Para magamit ang output VAT credit sa mga uncollected receivables, dapat may mga sumusunod na kondisyon: (a) naganap ang sale o exchange pagkatapos ng effectivity ng RR No. 3-2024; (b) ang sale ay on credit o on account; (c) may written agreement sa period to pay, tulad ng credit term na nakasaad sa invoice o anumang dokumentong nagpapakita nito; at (d) ang VAT ay hiwalay na nakasaad sa invoice [3].

Karagdagang kondisyon: ang customer o buyer ay dapat wastong nakilala sa Summary List of Sales sa quarter kung kailan ginawa ang sale [1]. Ang paglilimita ng lahat ng sales sa isang "various" account entry ay itinuturing na invalid compliance [1].

scored.query: Magkano ang excise tax na ipinapataw sa locally manufactured perfumes sa ilalim ng RR 9-2023?
scored.context:
[1] RR 9-2023, p.1 (2023)
REVENUE REGULATIONS NO. 9-2023 issued on August 3, 2023 prescribes the rules and regulations governing the imposition of Excise Tax on perfumes and toilet waters as provided under Section 150(b) of the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC) of 1997, as amended. There shall be levied, as sessed and collected a tax equivalent to twenty percent (20%) based on the wholesale price, net of Excise and Value-Added Tax (VAT), for locally manufactured perfumes and toilet waters. For imported articles, the Excise Tax of twenty percent (20%) shall be based on the value of importation used by the Bureau of Customs (BOC) in determining tariff and customs duties, net of Excise Tax and VAT. The Excise Tax shall be paid by the manufacturer or producer of locally manufactured perfumes and toilet waters.

---

[2] RR 9-2023, p.1 (2023)
The Excise Tax due on locally manufactured or produced perfumes and toilet waters shall be paid by the manufacture r or producer before removal from the place of manufacture/production and warehouse. Excise Tax herein imposed and based on selling price or other specified value of goods shall be referred to as "ad valorem tax." In the event that the brand owner(s) uses or engages in a toll manufacturing or subcontracting service or agreement, to facilitate the production of the excisable products, payment of Excise Tax shall be paid by the brand owner itself who owns the product or formulation before removals from their toll manufacturer's or subcontractor's production premises.

---

[3] RR 9-2023, p.1 (2023)
Unless otherwise specifically allowed, the return shall be filed and the Excise Tax paid by the manufacturer or producer of locally manufactured perfumes and toilet waters before removal of domestic products from place of production using eBIRForms or Form 2200-AN (Automobiles and Non-Essential Goods) via Electronic Filing and Payment System (eFPS), indicating the type of Tax marked as XG. In case of payment of the tax by any person other than the local manufacturer, the Excise Tax return shall likewise be accomplished and filed by such person indicating all the pertinent information therein. The Excise Tax due on locally manufactured or produced perfumes and toilet waters shall be paid by the manufacture r or producer before removal from the place of manufacture/production and warehouse.

scored.query: Kasama ba sa gross sales ng distribution utilities ang third-party charges base sa RMC 116-2024?
scored.context:
[1] RMC No. 116-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
For sale of services, including the sale of power, gross sales of Distribution Utility (DUs) and Electric Cooperatives (ECs) shall exclude the Value-Added Tax (VAT) and those amounts earmarked for payment to third (3rd) party or received as reimbursement for payment on behalf of another, which do not redound to the benefit of the seller as provided under relevant laws, rules or regulations. The DUs and ECs shall issue an invoice to the customers, which shall include the sale and transmission of electricity and ancillary services, including the VAT thereon of the Generation Companies (GenCos) and Transmission Companies (e.g. National Grid Corporation of the Philippines). However, the DUs and ECs shall not claim any Input Tax from these.

---

REVENUE MEMORANDUM CIRCULAR NO. 116-2024 issued on October 18, 2024, clarifies the provisions of Republic Act (RA) No. 11976 (Ease of Paying Taxes Act), applicable to the Power Industry. For sale of services, including the sale of power, gross sales of Distribution Utility (DUs) and Electric Cooperatives (ECs) shall exclude the Value-Added Tax (VAT) and those amounts earmarked for payment to third (3rd) party or received as reimbursement for payment on behalf of another, which do not redound to the benefit of the seller as provided under relevant laws, rules or regulations.

---

However, the DUs and ECs shall not claim any Input Tax from these. The proper claimant of Input Tax shall be the customers engaged in business based on the invoice to be issued by DUs/ECs. The pass-through charges of the Retail Electricity Supplier (RES) for the sale of power are the transmission and distribution charges. The RES shall not claim any input tax on the pass-through charges invoiced to the customers.

scored.query: Kailan lamang kwalipikado sa VAT zero-rating ang mga benta sa isang registered export enterprise?
scored.context:
[1] RMC No. 24-2022, p.2 (2022)
Sale of VAT-registered suppliers to registered export enterprises enjoying fiscal incentives under the CREATE Act shall be treated as VAT zero-rated. However, it shall only apply to goods and/or services directly and exclusively used in the registered project or activity of said registered export enterprise, for a maximum period of seventeen (17) years from the date of registration, unless otherwise extended under the Strategic Investment Priority Plan (SIPP). The enjoyment of VAT and duty incentives is reckoned from the registered export enterprise's date of registration and throughout the period as indicated in its Certificate of Registration.

---

[2] RMC No. 24-2022, p.3 (2022)
Only the portion of the expense directly and exclusively used by a registered export enterprise for its registered project or activity shall qualify for VAT zero-rating on local purchases, excluding those used for administrative purposes. The registered export enterprise concerned should adopt a method to best allocate goods or services purchased, e.g. for utilities, use of separate water and power meters for its registered project or activity or any method that may determine the allocation, such as area usage or ratio of utility expenses between cost of sales and administrative expenses as reflected in the prior year Audited Financial Statements.

---

[3] RMC No. 24-2022, p.6 (2022)
of paramount importance to validate whether the said requisites are duly complied with before availment of the VAT zero-rate incentive by the supplier of the registered export enterprise. Absence of prior approval from the BIR may result in the disallowance of the VAT zero-rated sale of the supplier. The IPA concerned shall issue annually a VAT zero percent (0%) certification only to registered export enterprises. The certification shall indicate the registered export enterprise's (i) registered export activity i.e., manufacturing, IT BPO; (ii) tax incentives entitlement under agreed terms and conditions with the validity period;
scored.answer:
Kwalipikado lamang sa VAT zero-rating ang mga benta sa isang registered export enterprise kung ang mga ito ay direktang at eksklusibong ginagamit sa rehistradong proyekto o aktibidad nito, at sa loob ng maximum na **17 taon** mula sa petsa ng rehistrasyon, maliban kung palawigin pa sa ilalim ng SIPP [1].

- Ang bahagi lamang ng gastos na direktang at eksklusibong ginagamit sa rehistradong proyekto ang kwalipikado — hindi kasama ang para sa administratibong layunin [2].
- Kailangan din ng prior approval mula sa BIR; kung wala ito, maaaring hindi payagan ang zero-rated na benta [3].

Hindi saklaw ng mga excerpt ang iba pang partikular na kondisyon o dokumentong maaaring kailanganin.

The BIR personnel coming from the concerned team of the BIR STRIKE Group shall be authorized to conduct covert surveillance acti vities on identified business establishments for possible violations of the provision of the National Internal Revenue Code ( NIRC) of 1997, as amended, based on a validly issued Mission Order (MO) signed by the Deputy Commissioner – Operations Group (DCIR-OG), Assistant Commissioner – Large Taxpayers Service (ACIR-LTS) or the concerned Regional Director (RD), and shall perform the following procedures: a. [1] RMO No. 14-2023 Digest FINAL, p.1 (2023)
REVENUE MEMORANDUM ORDER NO. 14-2023 issued on April 13, 2023 amends Revenue Memorandum Order (RMO) No. 5-2022 relative to the establishment and implementation of the Online Citizen/Client Satisfaction Survey (CCSS) for other BIR critical services under the Online Survey Feedback System (Phase 2) Project. All taxpayers/clients with completed transaction shall be encouraged to accomplish the online survey before the release of the document/transaction that was required/requested. The Revenue District Offices (RDOs)/concerned Divisions in the Revenue Regions and National Office/Large Taxpayers Divisions (LTD) of Cebu and Davao shall:

---

[2] RMO No. 14-2023 Digest FINAL, p.1 (2023)
A QR code shall also be made available for easy reference by taxpayers.  Prepare and submit to the statistician/planning officer/designated officer of the Region/Service a monthly Summary Report on Total Number of Transactions Per Critical Service , using the format provided in the Order, on or before the 10th day of each month following the reference period through their official e-mail address.  Receive on a weekly basis from the statistician/planning officer/ designated officer of the Region/Service the raw data on the taxpayers’ survey responses, specifically on the 10 th, 18 th and 25 th day of the current month and on the 3rd day of the following month.  Submit to the statistician/ planning officer/designated officer of the Region/ Service for consolidation,

---

[3] RMO No. 14-2023 Digest FINAL, p.1 (2023)

scored.query: Paano tinitiyak ang tax neutrality sa pagbili o pag-isyu ng mga Islamic bonds o Sukuk?
scored.context:
[1] RMC No. 81-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
REVENUE MEMORANDUM CIRCULAR NO. 81-2024 issued on July 18, 2024 provides the tax treatment of Sukuk (Islamic Bond) as Islamic banking arrangement pursuant to the Tax Neutrality Provision of Republic Act No. 11439 (An Act Providing for the Regulation and Organization of Islamic Banks) as implemented by Revenue Regulations No. 17-2020. Sukuk issued, structured in a Shari'ah-compliant manner, but with economic characteristics similar to bonds, are subject to the taxes per the Circular. The gain or profit in Sukuk is determined based on the specific structure and terms of the Sukuk issuance. It can be calculated through profit-sharing ratios, rental income, mark-up or price differentials, or the sale of underlying assets.

---

[2] RMC No. 81-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
It can be calculated through profit-sharing ratios, rental income, mark-up or price differentials, or the sale of underlying assets. The method of determining gain or profit depends on the contractual arrangements outlined in the Sukuk documentation. Gains or profits realized by Sukuk holders from Sukuk transactions with maturity of less than five years are subject to 20% Final Withholding Tax (FWT). On the other hand, those with maturity of five years or more are excluded from the gross income and are therefore exempt from Income Tax. In the case of Sukuk pre-termination, entire gains or profits realized by Sukuk holders, are subject to FWT with varying rates based on the remaining maturity thereof: Four (4) years to less than five (5) years - 5%;

---

[3] RMC No. 81-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
Any disposal or lease of the underlying asset, and execution of any additional instrument required in a Sukuk transaction, for the purpose of compliance with Shari'ah principles but which will not be required in a conventional bond transaction, shall be deemed excluded for taxation purposes. A Documentary Stamp Tax (DST) is imposed on all Sukuk instruments under Sections 176 and 179 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, (Tax Code) unless excepted under Section 199(g) of the same code. Guidelines and examples of some Sukuk structures that may be encountered in practice are provided in the Circular.

- Ang Sukuk na Shari'ah-compliant ngunit may economic characteristics na katulad ng bonds ay napapailalim sa mga buwis ayon sa Circular [1].
- Ang pag-dispose o pag-lease ng underlying asset, at ang mga karagdagang instrumento para sa Shari'ah compliance na hindi kailangan sa conventional bond, ay itinuturing na excluded sa taxation [3].
- May DST na ipinapataw sa lahat ng Sukuk instruments, maliban kung excepted sa ilalim ng Section 199(g) ng Tax Code [3].

Ang mga excerpt ay hindi naglalahad ng iba pang detalye kung paano mismo tinitiyak ang tax neutrality.

scored.query: May karapatan ba sa VAT zero-rating sa local purchases ang mga registered Domestic Market Enterprises sa ecozones?
scored.answer:
Hindi. Sa ilalim ng RMC No. 24-2022, ang mga Registered Business Enterprise (RBE) na categorized bilang Domestic Market Enterprises (DMEs) ay **hindi entitled sa VAT zero-rating** sa kanilang local purchases [1].

- Ang pagbenta ng goods o services sa isang registered DME ay **subject sa VAT na 12%** [1].
- Hindi na rin applicable ang "cross border doctrine" sa Ecozones o Freeport zones para sa VAT purposes dahil sa CREATE Act [2][3].

sentences.text: Hence, not all goods coming into, or services rendered within the Ecozones or Freeport shall be accorded VAT zero-rating.
RBEs which are categorized as Domestic Market Enterprises (DMEs) are not entitled to VAT zero-rating on local purchases.
Sale of goods or services to a registered DME shall be subject to VAT at 12%.

In addition, the following service enterprises, though duly accredited or licensed by any of the IPAs, are not entitled to VAT zero-rating on their local purchases of goods and/or services: • Customs brokerage;
• Trucking services; • Forwarding services;
• Janitorial services; • Security services;
• Insurance; • Banking and other financial services;
• Consumers' cooperatives;
• Credit unions; • Consultancy services;
• Retail enterprises; • Restaurants;

Thus, following the "cross border doctrine", the sale of goods and services by a VAT-registered seller to registered enterprises in these economic and freeport zones were treated as constructive export subject to zero-percent (0%) VAT.

The "cross border doctrine" as applied to Ecozones or Freeport zones has been rendered ineffectual and inoperative for VAT purposes with the passage of CREATE Act because of the following: a. Passage of RA No. 11534, or the CREATE Act, expressly providing that only those goods and services that are directly and exclusively used in the registered project or activity of Registered Business Enterprises (RBEs) qualify as VAT 0% local purchases;

The "cross border doctrine" as applied to Ecozones or Freeport zones has been rendered ineffectual and inoperative for VAT purposes with the passage of CREATE Act because of the following: a. Passage of RA No. 11534, or the CREATE Act, expressly providing that only those goods and services that are directly and exclusively used in the registered project or activity of Registered Business Enterprises (RBEs) qualify as VAT 0% local purchases;

b. Sections 294(E) and 295(D), Title Xlll of the Tax Code, as amended by the CREATE Act, and as implemented under Rule 2, Section 5, and Rule 18, Section 5, respectively, of the CREATE IRR, stating certain parameters for the availment of VAT zero-rating on local purchases of registered export enterprises, regardless of location;

scored.query: Ano ang mangyayari kung hindi kayang ihiwalay ang direct expenses sa administrative expenses para sa VAT zero-rating?
scored.context:
[1] RMC No. 24-2022, p.3 (2022)
infrastructure, utilities, and maintenance, repair and overhaul of equipment, and other expenditures directly attributable to the registered project or activity without which the registered project or activity cannot be carried out. Only the portion of the expense directly and exclusively used by a registered export enterprise for its registered project or activity shall qualify for VAT zero-rating on local purchases, excluding those used for administrative purposes.

---

[2] RMC No. 24-2022, p.3 (2022)
Only the portion of the expense directly and exclusively used by a registered export enterprise for its registered project or activity shall qualify for VAT zero-rating on local purchases, excluding those used for administrative purposes. The registered export enterprise concerned should adopt a method to best allocate goods or services purchased, e.g. for utilities, use of separate water and power meters for its registered project or activity or any method that may determine the allocation, such as area usage or ratio of utility expenses between cost of sales and administrative expenses as reflected in the prior year Audited Financial Statements.

---

[3] RMC No. 24-2022, p.3 (2022)
If the goods or services are used in both the registered project or activity and administration purposes and the proper allocation could not be determined, the purchase of such goods and services shall be subject to 12% VAT. For this purpose, services for administrative purposes, such as legal, accounting, and such other similar services, are not considered expenses directly attributable to and exclusively used in the registered project or activity. Cost items that fall under the “other expenditures” are costs that are indispensable to the project or activity, i.e., without which, the project or activity cannot proceed, and these include expenses that are necessary or required to be incurred depending on the nature of the registered project or activity of the export enterprise.
scored.answer:
Kung hindi kayang matukoy ang tamang alokasyon ng mga goods o services na ginagamit sa parehong registered project o activity at administrative purposes, ang pagbili ng mga ito ay sasailalim sa **12% VAT** [3].

- Ang mga serbisyong para sa administrative purposes, tulad ng legal at accounting services, ay hindi itinuturing na direktang nauugnay at eksklusibong ginagamit sa registered project o activity [3].
- Ang VAT zero-rating sa local purchases ay para lamang sa bahagi ng gastos na direktang at eksklusibong ginagamit ng registered export enterprise para sa registered project o activity nito [1][2].

Ang mga dokumento ay hindi nagbibigay ng iba pang detalye kung paano lutasin ang hindi matukoy na alokasyon maliban sa 12% VAT na panuntunan.

of paramount importance to validate whether the said requisites are duly complied with before availment of the VAT zero-rate incentive by the supplier of the registered export enterprise. scored.query: Ano ang panuntunan sa tax-free exchange of property kapag nagpalit ng ari-arian para sa shares of stock sa ilalim ng CREATE?
scored.context:
[1] 3089RMR 2-2002, p.1 (2002)
REVENUE MEMORANDUM RULING NO. 2-2002 issued on June 26, 2002 provides the guidelines in determining the substituted basis of property transferred and shares received, pursuant to a tax-free exchange of property for shares of stock under Section 40(C)(5) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997. The Ruling shall apply solely and exclusively to, and may be relied upon only in situations in which facts are substantially similar to the facts specified in the Ruling.

---

[2] 3089RMR 2-2002, p.1 (2002)
In the case where only one property is transferred, the substituted basis of the shares received by the Transferor is equal to the adjusted basis of the said property at the time of the transfer. To determine the substituted basis of each share, such aforementioned substituted basis shall be allocated pro rata among all the shares received by the Transferor in exchange for such property. When two or more properties are transferred, the proportionate number of shares issued for each property must first be determined. In the absence of express stipulation in the deed of assignment/exchange/transfer, the proportionate number of shares deemed issued for each property shall be determined as specified in the Rulings.

---

[3] 3089RMR 2-2002, p.1 (2002)
The Ruling shall apply solely and exclusively to, and may be relied upon only in situations in which facts are substantially similar to the facts specified in the Ruling. With respect to the determination of the substituted basis of the shares received by the Transferor, the basis of the stock or securities received by the transferor upon the exchange specified in the exception mentioned shall be the same as the basis of the property, stock or securities exchanged, decreased by the: (1) money received and (2) the fair market value of the other property received, and increased by (a) the amount treated as dividend of the shareholder and (b) the amount of any gain that was recognized on the exchange. Provided, that, the property received as “boot” shall have as basis its fair market value;
scored.answer:
Hindi saklaw ng mga dokumentong ibinigay ang tax-free exchange sa ilalim ng CREATE. Ang tanging panuntunang nakasaad dito ay ang **Revenue Memorandum Ruling No. 2-2002** (Hunyo 26, 2002), na nagbibigay ng guidelines sa pagtukoy ng substituted basis ng property na ipinagpalit at ng shares na natanggap sa tax-free exchange sa ilalim ng **Section 40(C)(5) ng NIRC of 1997** [1].

Sa ilalim nito:

- Kapag isang property lang ang ipinagpalit, ang substituted basis ng shares na natanggap ng Transferor ay katumbas ng adjusted basis ng property sa oras ng paglipat, at ito ay hinahati nang pro rata sa lahat ng shares na natanggap [2].
- Kapag dalawa o higit pang property ang ipinagpalit, dapat munang tukuyin ang proporsyonal na bilang ng shares para sa bawat property [2].
- Ang Ruling ay maaaring gamitin lamang sa mga sitwasyong halos katulad ng facts na nakasaad dito [1][3].

Wala pong nakasaad sa mga excerpt tungkol sa CREATE.

row.query: Ano ang panuntunan sa tax-free exchange of property kapag nagpalit ng ari-arian para sa shares of stock sa ilalim ng CREATE?

sagot.answer:
Hindi saklaw ng mga dokumentong ibinigay ang tax-free exchange sa ilalim ng CREATE. Ang tanging panuntunang nakasaad dito ay ang **Revenue Memorandum Ruling No. 2-2002** (Hunyo 26, 2002), na nagbibigay ng guidelines sa pagtukoy ng substituted basis ng property na ipinagpalit at ng shares na natanggap sa tax-free exchange sa ilalim ng **Section 40(C)(5) ng NIRC of 1997** [1].

Sa ilalim nito:

- Kapag isang property lang ang ipinagpalit, ang substituted basis ng shares na natanggap ng Transferor ay katumbas ng adjusted basis ng property sa oras ng paglipat, at ito ay hinahati nang pro rata sa lahat ng shares na natanggap [2].
- Kapag dalawa o higit pang property ang ipinagpalit, dapat munang tukuyin ang proporsyonal na bilang ng shares para sa bawat property [2].
- Ang Ruling ay maaaring gamitin lamang sa mga sitwasyong halos katulad ng facts na nakasaad dito [1][3].

Wala pong nakasaad sa mga excerpt tungkol sa CREATE.

The Ruling shall apply solely and exclusively to, and may be relied upon only in situations in which facts are substantially similar to the facts specified in the Ruling.

---

In the case where only one property is transferred, the substituted basis of the shares received by the Transferor is equal to the adjusted basis of the said property at the time of the transfer. When two or more properties are transferred, the proportionate number of shares issued for each property must first be determined. BACKGROUND On January 10, 2024, the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) issued Revenue Memorandum Circular (RMC) No. 5-2024 on the proper tax treatment of cross-border services in light of the Supreme Court (En Banc) Decision in Aces Philippines Cellular Satellite Corporation v. A Revenue Officer invoking the rule under the Aces Philippines case as a basis for their assessment must establish that the source of income from such cross-border services is within the Philippines, as follows: “[I]n ascertaining the income source, we must inquire into the property, activity, or service that produced the income. or where the inflow of wealth originated. ---

[3] RMC No. 24-2026, p.1 (2026) · OCR
No. 226680, promulgated on August 30, 2022 (Aces Philippines case). scored.query: Pwede pa bang gamitin ng National Government Agencies ang eTRA para magbayad ng penalties ayon sa RMC 1-2024?
scored.context:
[1] RMC No. 1-2024, p.1 (2024)
Likewise, the said RDOs shall undertake the reversal/correction in the Integrated Tax System-Collection and Bank Reconciliation (ITS-CBR)/ Internal Revenue Integrated System - Collection Remittance and Reconciliation (IRIS-CRR) of penalties paid by NGAs thru eTRA. As such, payment of penalties using eTRA shall not be recognized as part of the RDO's eTRA collection until the said penalties has been collected and paid in cash thru the AABs or any payment facilities available in the BIR.

---

[2] RMC No. 1-2024, p.1 (2024)
REVENUE MEMORANDUM CIRCULAR NO. 1-2024 issued on January 9, 2024 directs all National Government Agencies (NGAs) to discontinue the practice using the electronic Tax Remittance Advice (eTRA) for payment of penalties. The payment of the basic Withholding Tax shall be made through the eTRA System while the corresponding penalties, if any, shall be paid in cash thru the Authorized Agent Banks (AABs) or any payment facilities prescribed by the BIR.

---

[3] RMC No. 1-2024, p.1 (2024)
As a supplement, Revenue Memorandum Order No. 8-2003 identified Heads of Offices and Chief Accountan ts or other persons holding similar positions officially designated as such by the head of office as equally liable in the settlement of the said penalties. The Revenue District Offices (RDOs) and other concerned BIR offices are directed to strictly monitor the NGAs' compliance in the remittance of their Withholding Taxes with the corresponding penalties incurred, if any, due to late filing and payment on the part of the NGAs. Likewise, the said RDOs shall undertake the reversal/correction in the Integrated Tax System-Collection and Bank Reconciliation (ITS-CBR)/ Internal Revenue Integrated System - Collection Remittance and Reconciliation (IRIS-CRR) of penalties paid by NGAs thru eTRA.
scored.answer:
Hindi na. Ayon sa RMC No. 1-2024, ipinag-uutos sa lahat ng National Government Agencies (NGAs) na itigil ang paggamit ng electronic Tax Remittance Advice (eTRA) para sa pagbabayad ng penalties [2].

- Ang basic Withholding Tax ay dapat bayaran pa rin sa pamamagitan ng eTRA System [2].
- Ang mga penalties, kung mayroon man, ay dapat bayaran sa cash sa pamamagitan ng Authorized Agent Banks (AABs) o anumang payment facilities na itinakda ng BIR [2].
- Ang mga penalties na binayaran ng NGAs sa eTRA ay hindi kikilalanin bilang bahagi ng eTRA collection ng RDO hangga't hindi ito nakolekta at nabayaran sa cash [1].

row.query: Ano ang ipinagbabawal sa mga e-marketplace bago magkaltas ng 1% withholding tax sa sellers?

sagot.answer:
Hindi tahasang sinasabi ng mga excerpt na may "ipinagbabawal," pero may mga kondisyon bago magkaltas ng 1% withholding tax ang e-marketplace operators at DFSPs.

- Hindi applicable ang 1% withholding tax kung ang kabuuang gross remittances sa online seller/merchant para sa nakaraang taxable year ay hindi lumampas sa **₱500,000.00** [1].
- Nagsisimula ang obligasyon sa withholding kapag natanggap na ng e-marketplace operator o DFSP ang BIR-received SD na nagpapakitang lumampas na ang seller/merchant sa ₱500,000.00 threshold [2].
- Kailangan munang magsumite ng Certificate of Registration (BIR Form No. 2303) ang sellers/merchants bago payagang gumamit ng platform [3].

Hindi saklaw ng mga excerpt ang iba pang posibleng pagbabawal.

REVENUE REGULATIONS NO. 5-2024 issued on April 11, 2024, implements Sections 76(C), 112(C), 112(D), 204(C), 229 and 269(J) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended by Republic Act No. 11976 (Ease of Paying Taxes (EOPT) Act), on tax refunds. Ang **Revenue Regulations No. 5-2024** ang nagtatakda ng mga alituntunin sa pag-claim ng tax refund sa ilalim ng Ease of Paying Taxes (EOPT) Act [1].

- Inisyu ito noong **April 11, 2024**, at nagpapatupad ng mga probisyon ng Tax Code na inamyendahan ng RA 11976 (EOPT Act) [1].
- Saklaw nito ang mga tax credit/refund claim na **nagsisimulang isampa sa July 1, 2024** pataas [1].
- Kabilang sa mga saklaw nito ang risk-based approach sa VAT refund, ang 180-day processing ng mga claim maliban sa VAT refund, at ang refund ng unutilized excess income tax credit kapag dissolution o cessation of business [1][2].

Hindi saklaw ng regulasyong ito ang pagproseso ng mga refund claim na base sa final at executory judgment ng korte [3].

scored.context:
[1] RMO No. 46-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
REVENUE MEMORANDUM ORDER NO. 46-2024 issued on October 28, 2024, prescribes the policies, guidelines and procedures in the preparation and submission of Progress Report relative to the implementation of the programs/projects and activities in the BIR Strategic Plan for 2024-2028. The submission of Progress Report for the programs/projects and activities shall be on a quarterly basis. The offices responsible, as provided in the BIR Strategic Plan for 2024-2028, shall monitor the progress of implementation of the programs/projects and activities. The Summary Report of Hindrances and Solutions shall serve as input in the conduct of the BIR Annual Planning Session. The Quarterly Progress Report and Summary Report shall be prepared and submitted in accordance with the following schedules:

---

[2] RMO No. 46-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
The Quarterly Progress Report and Summary Report shall be prepared and submitted in accordance with the following schedules: Reports Submitted by Submitted to Deadlines Quarterly Progress Report (Annex A) 1st Quarter 2nd Quarter 3rd Quarter 4th Quarter ACIRs Regional Directors ACIR, PMS Attention: Chief, PPD Every 15th day of the month following the quarter Quarterly Summary Report (Annex B) 1st Quarter 2nd Quarter 3rd Quarter 4th Quarter ACIR, PMS thru Chief, PPD Commissioner Copy Furnish: Deputy Commissioners Every 25th day of the month following the quarter
scored.answer:
Sa ilalim ng RMO No. 46-2024, ang Quarterly Progress Report para sa BIR Strategic Plan 2024-2028 ay dapat isumite **tuwing ika-15 araw ng buwan kasunod ng bawat quarter** [2].

- Ang ulat ay isinusumite ng mga ACIR sa Regional Directors (ACIR, PMS, Attention: Chief, PPD) [2].
- Ang Quarterly Summary Report naman ay isinusumite tuwing ika-25 araw ng buwan kasunod ng quarter [2].

scored.query: Sino ang may pananagutan sa pag-verify ng accomplishments ng Taxpayer Awareness Program sa mga regional offices?
scored.context:
[1] RMO 52-2022_digest, p.1 (2022)
The region’s Client Support Unit (CSU) Head, under close supervision of the Assistant Regional Director , shall verify/validate the Points indicated by the RDO in the submitted TAP Accomplishment Report based on the documentation of taxpayer awareness activities compiled and submitted to the respective Regional Office by the RDOs (thru their Client Support Section Chief). The Total Points earned and the Average Points Per Month of the RDO for the semester shall be computed by the CSU Head and indicated in the RDO’s TAP Accomplishment Report, which shall be signed by the CSU Head and Certified True and Correct by the Assistant Regional Director. A copy of the validated/signed TAP Accomplishment Report shall be furnished to the respective Revenue District Officer.

---

[2] RMO 52-2022_digest, p.1 (2022)
The Assistant Regional Director of the Revenue Region, as the designated Sub-Social Media Team Head in the Regional Office who has the responsibility to ensure the accuracy and quality of the content published in the respective social media sites (per RMO No. 7-2022) shall directly oversee and supervise the verification and validation of the RDO’s TAP Accomplishment Report. The region’s Client Support Unit (CSU) Head, under close supervision of the Assistant Regional Director , shall verify/validate the Points indicated by the RDO in the submitted TAP Accomplishment Report based on the documentation of taxpayer awareness activities compiled and submitted to the respective Regional Office by the RDOs (thru their Client Support Section Chief).

---

[3] RMO 52-2022_digest, p.1 (2022)

The said Evaluation Report shall reflect the Ranking of the RDOs in the region based on the RDOs’ computed/validated Total Points and Average Points Per Month for 1st Semester/Calendar Year (as reflected in each RDO’s semestral TAP Accomplishment Report – Annex B1).
scored.answer:
Sa ilalim ng RMO 52-2022, ang **Client Support Unit (CSU) Head** ng rehiyon ang may pananagutan sa pag-verify/validate ng mga Points na nakasaad ng RDO sa kanyang TAP Accomplishment Report [1][2].

- Ginagawa ito ng CSU Head sa ilalim ng **close supervision ng Assistant Regional Director**, na siya ring direktang nangangasiwa sa verification at validation [1][2].
- Ang validated na report ay pipirmahan ng CSU Head at i-certify na True and Correct ng Assistant Regional Director, at bibigyan ng kopya ang RDO [1][3].
